question: Across the twelve calendar months of 2025, compute the Pearson correlation between monthly cancellation rate and average Delivered-order delivery time using SQL's CORR() function. Monthly cancellation rate = cancelled orders divided by all orders. Average delivery time = mean of delivery_time_min for Delivered orders with a non-null delivery duration only. Report the correlation coefficient, the number of months used, and whether that correlation alone supports a causal claim.

action.query:
SELECT 
    COUNT(*) AS months_used,
    CORR(monthly_cancellation_rate, avg_delivery_time_min) AS pearson_corr
FROM (
    SELECT 
        d.YEAR,
        d.MONTH,
        COUNT(o.ORDER_ID) AS total_orders,
        SUM(CASE WHEN f.IS_CANCELLED THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_orders,
        SUM(CASE WHEN f.IS_DELIVERED AND f.DELIVERY_TIME_MIN IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered_orders_with_time,
        AVG(CASE WHEN f.IS_DELIVERED AND f.DELIVERY_TIME_MIN IS NOT NULL THEN f.DELIVERY_TIME_MIN END) AS avg_delivery_time_min,
        CASE WHEN COUNT(o.ORDER_ID) > 0 THEN SUM(CASE WHEN f.IS_CANCELLED THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(o.ORDER_ID)::FLOAT ELSE NULL END AS monthly_cancellation_rate
    FROM ZOMATO_DLR.INTERMEDIATE.INT_DATE_FEATURES d
    LEFT JOIN ZOMATO_DLR.INTERMEDIATE.INT_ORDER_BASE o ON o.ORDER_DATE = d.DATE_DAY AND o.ORDER_DATE >= '2025-01-01' AND o.ORDER_DATE < '2026-01-01'
    LEFT JOIN ZOMATO_DLR.INTERMEDIATE.INT_ORDER_FULFILLMENT f ON o.ORDER_ID = f.ORDER_ID
    WHERE d.YEAR = 2025
    GROUP BY d.YEAR, d.MONTH
    HAVING COUNT(o.ORDER_ID) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN f.IS_DELIVERED AND f.DELIVERY_TIME_MIN IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
) sub

action.metrics: pearson correlation coefficient, number of months used
action.answer: The Pearson correlation coefficient between monthly cancellation rate and average delivered-order delivery time across the twelve calendar months of 2025 is -0.02003284030764907. This calculation used all 12 months in 2025. This correlation is very close to zero, indicating almost no linear relationship between the two variables at the monthly level. Furthermore, correlation alone does not support a causal claim; it only measures the strength and direction of a linear association, not causation.
